No—under those conditions, you would be extremely unlikely to see the Moon.

Although its geometric altitude is about 10.5°, it is only 3.45° from the Sun and just 0.09% illuminated. That is an exceptionally thin waning crescent, with the illuminated portion overwhelmed by bright daylight and atmospheric glare. The Moon’s angular separation from the Sun is also far below the roughly 10–15° separation generally needed for even experienced observers to attempt a naked-eye sighting of a very thin crescent.

At 10° altitude, atmospheric extinction and haze near the horizon make it harder still. An ordinary observer with unaided vision should assume it is not practically visible, despite being technically above the horizon. Specialized optical equipment, unusually clear conditions, and careful safety-conscious searching might detect it, but you should not look near the Sun without proper solar-viewing equipment.
